title: Edwards on beauty
hook: Jonathan Edwards saw God as the source of all beauty

segments.voice: Yesterday, Pascal and the reasons of the heart. Your line was the heart has reasons.

A young man walks alone in his father's pasture, looking up at the sky and the clouds. Later he wrote that something had changed in how he saw everything. God's glory seemed to show in the sun and moon and stars, in the clouds, the grass, the flowers, even in thunder, which used to frighten him. His name was Jonathan Edwards, a New England preacher.

For Edwards, beauty isn't decoration added on top of religion. It sits close to the center. God, he taught, is beautiful in himself, and every lovely thing in the world is a kind of echo or shadow of that beauty. A sunset is borrowed light. When Edwards tried to say what real goodness is, he talked about harmony: beings in loving agreement with one another, the way notes agree in a chord. Holiness, in his eyes, wasn't grim. It was lovely. He found that in the Bible. Psalm 19: "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork." Psalm 96: "O worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness." And the one request in Psalm 27, a psalm of David: "One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD." To behold. Not to argue about, not to prove. To look. Edwards could preach fiercely about judgment, and the same man wrote about God's glory in snow and sky and a field of flowers. Both were real to him. For Edwards, the change he called conversion was something like gaining a new sense, a taste for that beauty. He compared it to honey: you can hear honey described all day, but you only know its sweetness by tasting it. That closes a week of thinkers: Julian's mother love, Luther's freedom and his cross, Calvin's providence, Hooker's reason, Pascal's heart, and Edwards's beauty.
screen: `TO BEHOLD THE BEAUTY OF THE LORD.`

segments.voice: Let your eyes find one beautiful thing nearby, or one you can call up from memory: light on a wall, a tree outside the window, a face you love, the sound of rain. Behold it, the psalm's word, and stay with it longer than feels normal, coming back whenever your mind wanders. If you pray, you can let it lead you toward the one Edwards believed it echoes.
Edwards on beauty. Jonathan Edwards's teaching that God is beautiful, and that every beauty in the world reflects that beauty.
Your line: God is beautiful. Every sunset, for Edwards, is borrowed light. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Christians who read Jonathan Edwards, especially in Reformed and evangelical churches, speak of God's beauty and glory; across churches, Christians pray the Psalms of creation and worship "in the beauty of holiness" through music, art and attention to the natural world.

chat.says: Wasn't Jonathan Edwards just a fire-and-brimstone preacher?
options: He preached fiercely on judgment, but also taught that God is beautiful, echoed in all things.
Yes. He thought beauty was a distraction and kept his sermons on judgment only.
No. He never once preached about judgment; he only wrote about sunsets and flowers.
chat.meaning: Edwards could preach fiercely about judgment, yet taught that God is beautiful in himself, and every lovely thing is an echo of that beauty.
